name: Birsha
overview: Birsha is identified in Scripture as a male king who ruled over the city of Gomorrah. His role as King of Gomorrah is his primary distinguishing feature in the biblical record. No additional tribal affiliation or personal notes are provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Birsha means 'disagreeable in taste,' which may reflect a negative characteristic or perception, though this is not explicitly explained in the text. He is also known by the title 'King of Gomorrah,' indicating his royal authority over that city. Both names are referenced in Genesis 14:2.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Birsha beyond his status as King of Gomorrah. There are no recorded relatives or tribal connections associated with him.
scriptureSignificance: Birsha's significance lies in his position as a ruler of Gomorrah during the time described in Genesis 14:2. As a king of one of the cities involved in early biblical history, his role contributes to the understanding of the geopolitical landscape in the era of the patriarchs. Though details about his actions or character are sparse, his mention underscores the existence of organized city-states and kingships in the antediluvian world.
